question: How much of each salt was dissolved per litre to make the three forward osmosis draw solutions, and to what osmotic pressure?
expect: NaCl 35.0 g/L, MgSO4.7H2O 71.8 g/L, sodium acetate 79.4 g/L, each to 30 bar at 25 C (sec. 2.2)
rendered:
<document title="A Comparative Study of Forward Osmosis Systems: An Integrated Experimental, Modeling, and Techno-Economic Analysis">

=== page 1 ===
- Draw solutions were prepared to provide an initial nominal osmotic pressure of 30 bar at 25 °C, using analytical-grade salts: NaCl (35.0 g L^−1), MgSO4·7H2O (71.8 g L^−1), and sodium acetate (79.4 g L^−1).

=== page 2 ===
- Equal initial osmotic pressure (30 bar for all three draw solutions) was chosen to isolate draw solute chemistry as the variable under study, removing osmotic driving force as a confounding factor and giving each solution the same thermodynamic starting point.

=== page 3 ===
- Each of the three draw solutions was prepared to have an initial osmotic pressure of 30 bar at 25 °C, using the following concentrations:
- NaCl: 35.0 g L^−1
- MgSO4·7H2O: 71.8 g L^−1
- Sodium acetate: 79.4 g L^−1

The document does not provide the exact amount of each salt dissolved per litre to make the three forward osmosis draw solutions, but it does provide the concentrations of each salt in grams per litre.

To calculate the amount of each salt dissolved per litre, we can divide the concentration by the molar mass of each salt.

- NaCl: 35.0 g L^−1 / 58.44 g/mol = 0.599 mol L^−1
- MgSO4·7H2O: 71.8 g L^−1 / 246.48 g/mol = 0.291 mol L^−1
- Sodium acetate: 79.4 g L^−1 / 82.03 g/mol = 0.968 mol L^−1

These are the amounts of each salt dissolved per litre to make the three forward osmosis draw solutions.

Note: The molar masses of the salts were obtained from the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics.
